txt: Proposes rejecting the Commission proposal in its entirety, rather than amending individual provisions.
Proposes rejecting the Commission proposal in its entirety, rather than amending individual provisions.
Proposes rejecting the Commission proposal in its entirety, rather than amending individual provisions.
Proposes rejecting the Commission proposal in its entirety, rather than amending individual provisions.
Replaces decarbonisation with competitiveness in the Regulation's title, changing its stated policy emphasis.
Deletes decarbonisation from the title, retaining industrial capacity acceleration as the stated objective.
Adds loss of industrial autonomy, third-country dependencies and subsidised overcapacity to the recital's diagnosis, strengthening its emphasis on retaining industrial capabilities in the EU.
Recasts climate-related risks as natural disasters, criticises Green Deal costs and calls for reviewing, adapting or repealing policies considered harmful to industry.
Adds overcapacity and market distortions, and stresses that deindustrialisation magnifies the vulnerability created by economic dependencies. Removes the reference to the digital transition.
Adds tariffs, export restrictions, sanctions, investment distortions and industrial subsidies to the threats motivating EU industrial action.
Adds shipyards, maritime equipment manufacturers and their wider supply chain to the industrial sectors identified as strategically important.
Adds shipyards, maritime equipment manufacturers and their wider supply chain to the industrial sectors identified as strategically important.
Adds circular-economy activities, maritime manufacturing and railway locomotives and rolling stock to the recital's sectoral coverage.
Adds regulatory and administrative burdens on businesses, SMEs and farmers to the explanation of EU economic vulnerabilities.
Adds technical textiles for critical applications to the sectors recognised in the recital's industrial-security rationale.
Adds technical textiles for critical applications to the sectors recognised in the recital's industrial-security rationale.
Adds technical textiles for critical applications to the sectors recognised in the recital's industrial-security rationale.
Adds production relocation as a vulnerability and shifts the rationale towards economic, social and territorial cohesion and the development of quality employment.
Replaces the specific reference to Russia's aggression against Ukraine with a general reference to major armed conflicts.
Removes the automotive sector from the recital's list of sectors requiring action, narrowing its expressly identified industrial coverage.

cat: Foreign investment screening and strategic assets
txt: Adds a recital supporting investment screening to protect strategic assets, technology and employment, and favouring long-term productive investment over short-term extraction or transfers of control.
Adds a recital calling for lighter administration and faster permitting, extending support beyond decarbonisation projects and criticising the industrial impact of Green Deal regulation.
Adds a recital supporting new capacity, reshoring and the establishment or expansion of EU manufacturing to reinforce supply chains and quality employment.
Adds a recital linking industrial policy to defence production, maintenance, critical infrastructure and geographically diversified capacity, with particular attention to the EU's eastern flank.
Adds a recital calling for abolition of emissions trading and the use of all energy sources, presenting the green transition and pollution trading as favouring large business interests.
Defines resilience as a sustainable, fair and democratic transition and links strategic dependencies and market distortions to security, health and the green and digital transitions.

cat: Climate policy and international trade rules
txt: Adds a recital connecting decarbonisation to Article 191 TFEU and the GATT Article XX exceptions relevant to environmental and health protection.

Adds a recital advocating lignite production and reopening plants, including Ptolemaida 5, alongside abolition of emissions trading, energy-exchange arrangements and specified energy taxes or charges.

Adds a recital linking the Foreign Subsidies Regulation to industrial support, procurement and strategic projects, seeking to prevent benefits accruing to operators backed by distortive third-country subsidies.
Adds a recital advocating reopening and upgrading suspended nickel, ferronickel and cobalt facilities, citing LARCO in Greece and worker proposals for production and energy activities.

cat: Critical raw materials and supply security
txt: Adds a recital linking the Critical Raw Materials Act to industrialisation and decarbonisation, emphasising secure EU supply and reduced dependence on third countries.

cat: Better regulation and national industrial policy
txt: Adds a recital invoking better-regulation principles to limit administrative burdens, particularly for SMEs and mid-caps, and preserve Member States' ability to adapt industrial policy to national circumstances.
Adds a recital linking customs reform to origin verification, traceability and anti-circumvention, so European-preference measures benefit production actually located in the EU.

Adds long-term equity and patient-capital considerations, protection against speculative asset or technology transfers, and safeguards against opaque ownership structures circumventing investment conditions.
Specifies that the dependencies addressed in the recital are dependencies on imports, sharpening the description of the supply-security concern.
Adds a recital recognising outermost regions as industrial corridors and geostrategic footholds capable of strengthening EU supply-chain security and strategic autonomy.
Adds recognition of maritime manufacturing's contribution to resilience, defence readiness and decarbonisation, supporting its inclusion among beneficiaries of the Regulation.
Deletes the recital's quantified manufacturing-share objective and references tying industrial development to EU climate and energy targets.

Raises the manufacturing-share ambition from 20% to 25% and argues that climate policy should not impede reindustrialisation, advocating affordable energy, simpler rules, State aid flexibility and trade protection.
Adds an account of company closures and relocation, calling for firms to return to Europe and for support to new technologies and services that create employment.
Adds that a rising manufacturing share caused by contraction elsewhere in the economy should not count as progress towards the 20% objective.
Emphasises a decarbonised industrial base, quality employment and renewable-based electrification, framing economic resilience and climate objectives as mutually reinforcing.
Deletes the 20%-of-GDP-by-2035 objective and the associated sentence linking facilitation of manufacturing projects to that target.
Adds support for resilient production and protection against imports not meeting European standards, reframing project development around industrial capacity and internal-market objectives.
Replaces the 20% manufacturing-share target with better investment conditions and monitoring through investment, productivity, permitting times and energy-cost indicators.
Rejects an EU quantitative manufacturing-share target, attributes industrial decline partly to regulatory and emissions costs, and prioritises affordable energy and lower business burdens.
Recasts the recital's climate-policy framing to criticise pursuing targets regardless of cost and to prioritise affordable, competitive energy prices.
Deletes the sentence setting a 20% manufacturing share of EU GDP by 2035, removing the quantified ambition from the recital.
Replaces the manufacturing-share objective with an ambition to reverse decline and increase manufacturing's growth rate by an average of 1% annually.
Replaces the 20%-of-GDP manufacturing target with a priority objective of strengthening industrial competitiveness.

Adds a recital linking industrialisation to affordable energy, lower administrative burdens, regulatory stability and predictable taxation, and calling for progress to be assessed against those enabling conditions.

Adds circularity and resource efficiency to the industrial rationale and describes projects supplying secondary materials, products or components as substitutes for primary inputs or newly manufactured goods.

Adds a recital calling for beneficiaries across procurement, support, investment and acceleration measures to respect collective bargaining, quality jobs, training and worker information and consultation throughout supply chains.
Adds a recital advocating that European-preference measures be restricted to EU-27 production to rebuild industrial value chains, retain expertise and reduce external dependencies.

Adds a recital distinguishing genuine decarbonisation from closure and replacement by imports, favouring modernisation, competitive low-carbon energy, efficiency, recycling and retained EU production.
Adds a recital limiting market-access restrictions to evidenced capability gaps and requiring targeted, proportionate measures consistent with international obligations, including WTO rules.
Adds a recital opposing requirements unless they are shown not to increase living or business costs, placing affordability conditions on the industrial-policy rationale.

Adds a recital presenting electrification and grid investment as central to industrial competitiveness and decarbonisation, referencing the 32% electricity-share benchmark for 2030 and indicative 46% target for 2040.
Adds a recital calling for anticipation and management of industrial restructuring and job displacement, using EU adjustment, social and just-transition funds to support affected workers.

cat: EU origin and substantive value creation
txt: Adds a recital rejecting assembly, packaging or final transformation alone as proof of EU origin where the main production steps, technology, labour and value added remain outside the EU.
Deletes the recital explaining why cross-border industrial challenges and fragmented national measures justify harmonised EU action.
Replaces the fragmentation rationale with a common European framework for accelerating and protecting high-emitting industries while preserving compatible national measures.

cat: Energy mixes and fair access to demand measures
txt: Adds safeguards against origin and low-carbon requirements favouring Member States with cheaper energy or better infrastructure, seeking a more even distribution of industrial demand and investment.
Adds concerns that divergent national screening standards permit third-country investors to exploit weaker scrutiny or make investments inconsistent with long-term industrial objectives.
Replaces the detailed warning against fragmented national action with a shorter rationale emphasising coordinated demand policy and an accurate definition of low-carbon production.
Adds that historically or structurally different national energy mixes should not create unequal access to the lead markets established by the Regulation.
Adds conditions that harmonised measures remain proportionate, avoid unnecessary administrative burdens and reflect sectoral characteristics and existing national frameworks.
Replaces decarbonisation with recovering competitiveness in the recital's description of the industrial challenge.
Adds a recital presenting support to strategic value chains as necessary for reducing dependencies and preserving industrial capacity, autonomy and economic and political sovereignty.

Removes the emissions-share and decarbonisation-investment framing, adds a competitiveness rationale centred on energy costs, and calls for national spending flexibility and reconsideration of EU fiscal constraints.

cat: Clean technology deployment and industrial investment
txt: Adds coordinated deployment of clean technologies and related supply chains to enable existing industrial sites and technology suppliers to scale up and invest together.
Adds support for a technology-neutral approach to emissions-reduction investment, allowing industries to choose effective solutions while maintaining competitiveness.
Adds that reversing industrial decline requires lower energy costs, investment finance and action against unfair competition.
Adds recognition that emissions remain high despite substantial industrial modernisation investments, qualifying the recital's account of decarbonisation progress.
Deletes the emissions-share and pollution-reduction explanation and reframes decarbonisation as an obligation contributing to industrial cost pressures.
Adds insufficient recognition of nuclear energy's role in affordable, reliable supply to the factors explaining pressure on energy-intensive industries.
Adds economic security and identifies defence, renewables, maritime and aerospace among strategic downstream sectors depending on energy-intensive industries.
Attributes the acceleration of industrial difficulties to earlier political choices, replacing a more neutral account of growing pressures.
Adds electrification to the recital's description of the industrial transition and investment challenge.

Adds a recital describing lost metals and chemicals production, low capacity utilisation, import dependence and stalled decarbonisation investment as risks to economic security, climate objectives and employment.

cat: Critical raw materials and industrial feasibility
txt: Adds a recital warning that industrial targets require secure, diversified and competitive raw-material supplies, supporting stronger European value chains while avoiding new import dependencies.
Adds low-carbon technologies and explicitly highlights dependence on imports from high-emissions production systems, including China, in the recital's supply-chain concerns.

cat: Renewables, fossil dependencies and unfair trade
txt: Adds reduction of fossil-fuel import dependence, renewable transition and strategic autonomy, while expanding the description of coercive, unfair and illegal practices affecting supply chains.
Adds recognition that EU manufacturing of electricity-grid technologies and digital solutions supports energy security, technological sovereignty and reduced dependencies.
Adds emphasis on electricity-grid technologies as enabling clean-energy integration, industrial electrification and energy-system security and resilience.
Adds that joint clean-technology deployment at energy-intensive sites can create predictable demand, support EU manufacturing scale-up and improve the business case for decarbonisation.
Replaces the stronger statement of technologies' necessity for climate targets with a broader role for net-zero and low-carbon technologies in the energy transition.
Broadens the recital to low-carbon technologies and energy diversification while removing its stronger statements on meeting climate targets and sectoral decarbonisation.
Adds that progress is slow partly because practical, viable technological solutions remain delayed, qualifying the account of transition challenges.

cat: Energy security, electrification and market distortions
txt: Adds energy security and electrification and expands the warning about unfair practices and systemic market distortions affecting net-zero technologies.
Adds a recital describing foreign subsidies, local-content policies and lost shipbuilding activity as threats to European maritime equipment production, innovation, skills and value-chain resilience.
Adds a recital calling for implementation to accelerate renewable generation, battery storage, grids and renewable electricity sourcing as strategic industrial and energy-security assets.
Adds agricultural, forestry and food-industry residues, bioeconomy research and new materials to the biomass rationale, subject to biodiversity, land-use and food-security safeguards.

cat: Pulp, paper and sustainable secondary materials
txt: Adds low-carbon pulp and paper, bio-based production and defossilisation, linking local quality jobs and fossil independence to secondary materials that avoid additional pressure on forests and biodiversity.
Adds opposition to a new biomass-use hierarchy or cascading principle, arguing that existing renewable-energy sustainability rules already govern agricultural biomass and by-products.
Adds a call for Commission preparation of EU-origin and low-carbon requirements for chemicals derived from low-carbon or sustainable carbon sources.
Adds bio-based production and defossilisation, stressing their contribution to non-relocatable green jobs and reduced dependence on fossil resources.
Deletes the recital explaining automotive decarbonisation investment, electric-vehicle value chains and related EU industrial vulnerabilities.
Adds hybrid vehicles, the role of automotive supplier SMEs, lifecycle emissions, reparability and recycling, and the employment and production-site consequences of the sector's structural crisis.

Criticises the policy-driven pace of electrification and Chinese competition, and advocates support for EU-made electric, fuel-cell and renewable or low-carbon-fuel vehicles rather than an exclusively electric pathway.
Recasts automotive difficulties around policy-driven electrification, consumer demand and competitiveness, calling for review of the framework and equal treatment of competing vehicle technologies.
Adds regional supplier structures, software, automated driving and new production and interior materials to the description of changes in automotive value chains.
Emphasises the sector's employment contribution and existing job losses, warning that further displacement could create a major social crisis.

cat: Affordable clean vehicles and public support
txt: Adds that procurement and support schemes should make cleaner vehicles accessible to all, linking industrial demand measures to a just and democratic transition.
Adds an urgent call for a European action plan identifying practical steps to develop and support the automotive sector.
Removes the specific attribution of changing vehicle value shares to batteries, e-powertrains and electronics, leaving a more general description of declining EU content.
Adds environmental objectives alongside climate objectives to the recital's account of automotive investment and the risks associated with industrial dependence.
Adds tyres to the vehicle-component value chain identified in the recital, extending the industrial rationale beyond batteries, powertrains and electronics.
Adds tyres to the vehicle-component value chain identified in the recital, extending the industrial rationale beyond batteries, powertrains and electronics.
Describes automotive investment as compelled by misguided policies and removes the final climate-goals reference, recasting the recital as a criticism of regulatory pressure.

Adds a recital covering shipbuilding, repair, conversion, recycling and equipment, highlighting clean maritime technologies and the threat from subsidised foreign competition to EU capacity, skills and climate objectives.
Adds a recital recognising material recovery as strategically important and calling for low-carbon product assessments to reflect emissions avoided through secondary raw materials.
Adds a recital recognising technical textiles for health, defence, aerospace and critical infrastructure, linking retained EU production to skills, traceability and safety verification.

Adds a recital calling for demand measures for vessels and maritime equipment to counter foreign distortions and preserve EU capacity and naval capabilities, without prejudicing defence procurement rules or national competences.
Adds a recital describing subsidised foreign shipbuilding and local-content policies as threats to EU maritime manufacturing, innovation, skilled employment and value-chain resilience.
Adds a recital describing subsidised foreign shipbuilding and local-content policies as threats to EU maritime manufacturing, innovation, skilled employment and value-chain resilience.

Adds a recital warning that maritime origin requirements could raise costs and delay renewal and decarbonisation, calling for prior impact assessment and consultation, including shipowners and operators.

cat: Strategic sectors and industrial supply chains
txt: Adds a recital recognising chemicals, plastics, glass, pharmaceuticals and maritime manufacturing as strategic industrial sectors whose European supply chains require reinforcement.
Adds a recital identifying maritime manufacturing as essential to the EU industrial base and exposed to distortive global competition threatening its competitiveness and resilience.

Adds a recital supporting strategic treatment and local-content measures for textiles, linking decarbonisation, public procurement and critical applications to pressure from unfair competition and direct-to-consumer imports.
Adds a recital supporting recognition of repair, reuse, remanufacturing and recycling as strategic activities eligible for accelerated permitting and investment support.
Adds a recital proposing strategic status and accelerated permitting for low-carbon pulp and paper, emphasising circular material loops, local employment and alternatives to fossil-based materials.
Adds reliance on existing authorities and structures, where appropriate, to avoid duplicative administrative layers and costs in permitting.
Adds proportionate implementation for SMEs and entities with limited administrative capacity to the recital's permitting rationale.

cat: Permitting contact points and legislative coherence
txt: Replaces the competent-authority wording with a single point of contact and aligns the approach with the proposed environmental-assessment acceleration framework.
Specifies that each Member State designates a national authority to coordinate permitting and take the comprehensive decision, while referring to both national and European procedures.
Adds modern solutions and innovation to the means by which industrial permitting should be improved.
Replaces the emphasis on procedural unpredictability and complexity with under-resourced authorities, calling for sufficient staff and finance to perform permitting tasks.

cat: Interoperability, origin guidance and compliance evidence
txt: Adds a recital supporting integrated digital portals, data reuse and timeline monitoring, an Access2Markets origin-information tool, protection for reliance on official guidance and standardised self-declarations.
Adds a recital calling for coherent application with environmental-assessment and grid legislation so project promoters face a single, consistently implemented set of procedures.
Replaces the Business Wallet rationale with limits on Commission use of collected data and national control over sensitive industrial information, including security-based non-disclosure.
Adds digital submission and transmission of related authority requests and decisions, extending digitalisation beyond the initial application.
Softens mandatory-sounding language around single access points and Business Wallets and emphasises coordination with existing national measures.
Adds reduction of burdens for both businesses and public administrations as an express objective of the digital permitting arrangements.
Adds national infrastructure alongside EU digital infrastructure to the systems that single access points should reuse where possible.
Adds a recital calling for authorities to reuse data and documents through single access points or Business Wallets, subject to validity, confidentiality and data-protection requirements.
Adds a recital calling for reachable human contact persons alongside digital channels, particularly to assist SMEs and first-time project applicants.
Adds a recital calling for an SME helpdesk within the single digital access point to support permit applications and related compliance.
Adds that a single application coordinates procedures but does not merge legal bases or alter the substantive conditions attached to installation, site or emissions permits.
Adds designation of single points of contact at the relevant administrative level to coordinate the permit-granting procedure.
Clarifies that single permitting must respect existing environmental legislation and does not exempt industrial operators from environmental obligations.

Adds a recital supporting deemed approval after an authority misses its deadline and equivalent documentary evidence, except where EU law requires an express decision or otherwise prevents tacit approval.
Adds a recital supporting national priority-area frameworks that favour brownfield reuse over greenfield expansion while safeguarding environmental law, communities and biodiversity.
Deletes the recital linking industrial projects to the common environmental-assessment acceleration framework and its dedicated strategic-project toolbox.
Broadens the reference to net-zero and low-carbon projects while deleting the particular justification based on energy-intensive decarbonisation projects' climate and security contribution.
Adds sectoral decarbonisation, low-carbon processes, resource efficiency and circularity to the contributions relevant to accelerated project treatment.
Adds joint energy-intensive industry and clean-technology projects to the project types recognised in the environmental-assessment acceleration rationale.

Replaces acceleration terminology with streamlining, removes the call for even faster assessments in some sectors and adds consultation of environmental NGOs and relevant public agencies on the toolbox.
Adds low-carbon technologies alongside the existing technology coverage in the recital on environmental-assessment acceleration.

Adds equal permitting treatment for projects combining industrial modernisation or decarbonisation with clean-technology deployment and supply chains, with Commission criteria to support eligibility decisions.

Adds that proportionate, mitigated temporary impacts should not alone block decarbonisation projects delivering substantial net environmental improvement, while retaining health and ecosystem safeguards.
Adds that equal permitting treatment should apply regardless of the technology used to achieve an industrial project's decarbonisation objectives.
Adds low-carbon technologies throughout the recital's references to the production and supply chains benefiting from streamlined industrial permitting.
Deletes the word 'of' in the recital's reference to decarbonisation projects, making a drafting adjustment without introducing a distinct permitting condition.

Adds a recital supporting exemption from nitrogen-emissions assessment for industrial upgrades and related CO2 infrastructure where they structurally reduce those emissions, to avoid delaying cleaner replacement capacity.

Adds a recital arguing that temporary construction emissions should not prevent investment in industrial changes or extensions whose nitrogen-reduction benefits substantially outweigh those emissions.

cat: Social conditionality of procurement and support
txt: Adds quality-job objectives, compliance with environmental and labour law and collective agreements, and conditions maintaining supported EU production and employment for at least five years after final payment.

cat: Social conditionality and retention of production
txt: Adds labour-law, collective-agreement and ILO conditions for support, alignment with the Clean Industrial Deal State Aid Framework and five-year retention of supported EU capacity and employment.
Adds capacity mechanisms exclusively deploying net-zero technologies, especially battery storage, to the auction concept so they are covered by the industrial demand framework.

cat: SMEs, mid-caps and long-term industrial investment
txt: Adds particular benefits for EU SMEs and mid-caps and links public intervention to reindustrialisation and investment aligned with long-term industrial objectives.
Adds transparent procurement and European-preference purchasing as tools for accelerating EU industrial capacity.
Deletes the decarbonisation objective attached to support schemes and the recital's explanation of auctions as a demand tool for net-zero technologies and EU components.
Adds low-carbon downstream products in their design or use phase and extends the description of demand measures to incentive schemes.
Adds low-carbon downstream products in their design or use phase and extends the description of demand measures to incentive schemes.
Adds technological neutrality and a level playing field between eligible decarbonisation solutions to the principles governing public intervention.
Deletes 'where appropriate', making the recital's expectation that procurement foster economic security and supply-chain resilience less qualified.

Adds a recital supporting non-price procurement criteria, European innovative products and public-private investment partnerships, with closer coordination of industrial, trade, research and procurement policies.
Adds a recital advocating a broad origin concept covering customs-union, trade-agreement and GPA partners, to preserve international commitments and diversified, reliable supply chains.
Adds a recital recognising tyres as strategic vehicle products and supporting procurement and aid criteria based on fuel-efficiency and wet-grip classes under the Tyre Labelling Regulation.
Adds a recital supporting consideration of tyre performance in procurement and support schemes, linking rolling resistance to energy consumption, road safety and EU competitiveness.
Adds a recital calling for extra costs from origin and low-carbon requirements to be reflected in procurement price lists, unit prices and estimates, protecting contractual economic balance.
Adds a recital linking incentives to actual EU value added and gradual introduction, while preserving national tax competence, technology neutrality and State aid compliance.
Adds a recital calling for origin and low-carbon requirements to be timed against market capacity and product availability, to avoid access barriers and unintended distortions.
Adds a recital calling for sector-specific impact assessment before extending the Regulation's scope.

cat: Think Small First and SME proportionality
txt: Adds a recital opposing disproportionate complexity, reporting and compliance costs for SMEs, with predictable requirements proportionate to their capacities.
Deletes the recital describing the EU's open investment environment, procurement commitments, exceptions and treatment of third-country origin equivalence.
Deletes the recital describing the EU's open investment environment, procurement commitments, exceptions and treatment of third-country origin equivalence.

Replaces the exclusion-oriented approach with affirmative, targeted recognition by delegated act, distinguishing national treatment from EU-origin status and adding reciprocity, supply-security and anti-circumvention conditions.

cat: Trusted partners, reciprocity and carbon costs
txt: Adds support for OECD GPA partners, especially for nuclear and defence supply chains, while conditioning preferences on reciprocal access and avoiding significant net carbon-cost advantages over EU producers.

Adds trusted partnerships and customs unions, continuous market-access assessment, time for compliance discussions before exclusion, and delegated-act inclusion following new agreements or GPA accession.
Adds explicit compliance with WTO and other international procurement agreements, including their procedures and conditions for restrictions and the treatment they guarantee partner countries.
Replaces the recital's discussion of procurement commitments and exceptions with a product-origin rationale pursuing economic security, industrial resilience and quality employment.
Adds equivalent-origin treatment for trusted agreement partners and particular attention to integrating candidate countries, especially Ukraine, into European industrial value chains.
Adds that customs-union partners' goods, assembly and manufacturing operations should receive equivalent treatment under Chapter III, subject to the Article 8 and 9 safeguards.

Adds an inclusion-and-exclusion assessment approach linked to economic security, an exception concerning investments by foreign subsidiaries, and reinforcement of measures protecting the EU steel industry.

cat: Opt-in equivalence and controlled investment vehicles
txt: Replaces exclusion-oriented wording with assessment for third-country inclusion and qualifies the intra-EU investment safeguard where an EU-established entity remains controlled by a third-country person or company.
Adds recognition of exceptions necessary to protect human, animal or plant life or health under the GPA, broadening the stated grounds relevant to industrial measures.
Adds assessment of both inclusion and exclusion of third countries and changes the recital's Commission-action wording from 'will' to 'should'.
Replaces the reference to assessing exclusion with inclusion, shifting the recital towards an affirmative eligibility assessment, although the remaining wording is not fully harmonised.
Changes the recital from assessing grounds for third-country exclusion to assessing grounds for inclusion in equivalent-origin treatment.

cat: Social, climate and reciprocal equivalence conditions
txt: Adds a recital requiring delegated-act recognition of equivalence against cumulative market-access, competition, labour, human-rights, climate, comparable demand-measure and anti-circumvention conditions.

cat: Automatic recognition of trusted partner countries
txt: Adds a recital supporting partner status from entry into force for countries meeting GPA, EU trade or customs agreement, International Energy Agency membership and Paris Agreement criteria.
Adds a recital arguing that common commercial policy must not absorb industrial-policy or national competences, and supporting protection of strategic industries and prevention of carbon leakage.
Adds a recital favouring early, favourable assessment of deeply integrated trade and association partners, customs-union partners and EEA countries, with particular priority for EEA participants.

Adds a recital requiring origin, carbon and investment measures to respond to demonstrated risks and remain proportionate, warning against indiscriminate restrictions that disrupt supply chains and raise costs.

Adds a recital opposing equivalent-origin treatment for countries persistently facilitating sanctions evasion or materially supporting serious security threats, with evidence and seriousness thresholds for exclusion.
Adds a recital supporting equivalent-origin treatment for Ukrainian goods and goods from non-EU EEA countries across all requirements and preference mechanisms.
Adds a recital combining trusted-partner cooperation, Ukraine integration and respect for agreements with safeguards against opaque ownership and minimal-processing circumvention.
Adds a recital favouring European countries and trusted partners such as Japan, South Korea and Canada, with priority assessment and a delegated act within six months of entry into force.

Adds a recital supporting checks on ownership, control, component and technology origin and substantive value added to prevent limited relocation or assembly being used to obtain equivalent-origin treatment.
Adds a recital supporting EU-origin treatment for locally transformed resources from associated overseas countries and territories, subject to social, environmental and anti-circumvention safeguards.

Adds delegated-act recognition of further agreement partners against reciprocity, supply diversification, anti-circumvention and Paris Agreement criteria, with a first act within six months and removal if conditions lapse.

Adds a recital arguing that international agreements and equivalence arrangements must preserve the substance of EU-origin, resilience and supply-security requirements and allow distinctions based on environmental performance.

Adds a recital requiring consistent compliance with GATT, subsidy, investment and services agreements across origin, workforce and sourcing conditions, seeking to reduce retaliation and dispute risks.
Adds a recital calling for reasoned Commission assessment of third-country, Parliament or Council requests for equivalence within one year of receipt.

Adds a recital defending Member States' ability to protect security, industrial capacity, climate, energy supplies and environmental interests against constraints arising from trade and investment openness.

Adds a recital calling for unanimous Council approval of each inclusion, based on cumulative reciprocity, security, social, environmental, carbon-pricing and anti-circumvention conditions, with suspension when conditions fail.
Deletes the recital supporting progressive integration of candidate and potential candidate countries into EU policies, programmes and the internal market.
Deletes the recital supporting progressive integration of candidate and potential candidate countries into EU policies, programmes and the internal market.
Deletes the recital supporting progressive integration of candidate and potential candidate countries into EU policies, programmes and the internal market.

Recasts candidate-country integration around formal accession and effective application of equivalent environmental, social, fiscal and competition standards, opposing premature extension of internal-market benefits.
Adds conditions requiring monitoring of accession criteria and negotiations in relevant areas, alongside protection of the EU labour market.

Adds a recital conditioning equivalence on updated climate commitments, sustained emissions reductions, fossil-fuel phase-out, carbon pricing and climate finance, with safeguards against carbon leakage and CBAM circumvention.
Adds a recital determining software origin by substantive development activities and EU value added, with Commission methodologies for multi-country development and anti-circumvention.
Adds a recital opposing partner-origin treatment where producers are controlled from a country with over 40% of sectoral global capacity or over half the parts' value comes from that country.
Adds a recital calling for timely finance and better coordination of EU instruments to support manufacturing, clean technologies and resilient supply chains, particularly for SMEs and mid-caps.
Adds a recital supporting investigation and targeted suspension or withdrawal of equivalence where minor processing or relocation creates insufficient genuine local manufacturing value.
Adds a recital proposing a facility to facilitate access to existing EU grants, loans, guarantees, equity and blended finance for industrial capacity, decarbonisation and resilience projects.
Deletes the recital recognising comparable third-country industrial preferences and addressing acceptance of partner-country local-content requirements in reciprocal relationships.
Deletes the recital recognising comparable third-country industrial preferences and addressing acceptance of partner-country local-content requirements in reciprocal relationships.
Deletes the recital recognising comparable third-country industrial preferences and addressing acceptance of partner-country local-content requirements in reciprocal relationships.

cat: Effective reciprocity and domestic value creation
txt: Recasts recognition of partner-country industrial preferences as conditional on effective reciprocal market access, comparable social and environmental conditions and genuine EU production, skills, employment and research benefits.
Adds inclusion of countries meeting the Regulation's conditions in a partner list and removal when those conditions are no longer fulfilled.
Conditions acceptance of partner-country local-content requirements on proportionality and comparable reciprocal treatment and effective market access for EU operators.
Adds protection of procedural data and prospective solutions against external interference to the recital on reciprocal industrial measures.
Adds a recital supporting a uniform EU-average electricity reference factor for low-carbon assessments to avoid unequal treatment arising from national electricity mixes.
Adds a recital prioritising deeper integration with key partners and rules-based trade when defining equivalent-origin content across preference regimes.

Adds EU-origin emphasis, coherent coverage of concrete, mortar, cement and clinker, and recognition of recycled inputs to support EU production and reduce imported emissions and primary-material dependence.

cat: Chemical demand measures and enabling conditions
txt: Adds sustainable-carbon requirements and fertiliser, selected plastics and chemicals coverage, recognises biodegradability and compostability, and links demand measures to competitive-energy and other supply-side support.
Adds a whole-building and infrastructure approach to decarbonisation, supporting material efficiency, offsite construction and lightweight methods alongside lower-carbon individual materials.
Adds sustainable-carbon requirements and Net-Zero Industry Act technologies, conditioning market opportunities on competitive energy, infrastructure, technologies and inputs for EU producers.

Adds gradual sectoral introduction reflecting capacity, national starting points and costs, with low-carbon requirements delayed until calculation methodologies exist and producers have time to adapt.
Extends the demand rationale to net-zero technologies, fertilisers, selected plastics and chemicals, while linking low-carbon competitiveness to adequate supply-side support and competitive energy.
Adds origin requirements, plastics, flat glass, chemicals, pharmaceuticals and grids, quality manufacturing employment and reassessment as industrial dependencies evolve.

cat: Energy mixes and equal market access
txt: Adds that all EU companies should benefit equally from demand measures regardless of their Member State's energy mix.
Adds sustainable-carbon requirements, flat glass, plastics, net-zero technologies including wind projects, and end-market measures for fertilisers and selected chemicals.
Adds requirements concerning sustainable carbon sources and end-market measures for fertilisers, selected plastics applications and selected chemicals.
Adds origin requirements for concrete and mortar, plastics, flat glass, cast and forged products, and net-zero technologies including wind projects.
Adds that steel should also face EU-origin requirements where public intervention can materially preserve European steelmaking capacity.
Strengthens the origin requirement, adds plastics and flat glass, and includes electrification in the industrial demand rationale.
Adds Net-Zero Industry Act technologies, expressly including wind-energy projects, to the demand-measure rationale.
Adds Net-Zero Industry Act technologies, including wind projects, while retaining low-carbon production in the demand-measure rationale.
Adds iron and plastics, expressly including water pipes, to the materials addressed by demand measures.
Adds iron and copper to the materials covered by the recital's industrial demand rationale.
Adds fertilisers to the sectors identified for industrial demand measures.
Removes motor vehicles from the recital's expressly identified downstream demand coverage.

cat: Chemical value chains and tailored measures
txt: Adds a recital supporting chemical-sector demand measures differentiated by market segment and covering substantive production steps throughout upstream and downstream value chains.

Adds a recital requiring assessment of necessity, proportionality and effectiveness before new chemical demand measures, distinguishing individual products and value chains rather than treating the sector uniformly.

cat: Glass, mineral wool and gypsum coverage
txt: Adds a recital supporting demand measures for glass, glass fibre, mineral wool and gypsum-based products and their downstream industrial applications.

Adds a recital conditioning aluminium and other energy-intensive product requirements on clear methodologies, verification capacity and realistic transitions, reflecting electricity costs, production routes and recycled inputs.
Adds that requirements should remain compatible with retained EU production, industrial employment and competitiveness.
Adds maritime manufacturing to the sectoral rationale and calls for technological neutrality in applying industrial requirements.
Adds maritime manufacturing to the strategic sectors addressed by the recital's demand requirements.
Adds maritime manufacturing to the strategic sectors addressed by the recital's demand requirements.
Adds maritime manufacturing and replaces the option of applying either requirement or both with wording favouring combined requirements.
Replaces the alternatives allowing either origin or low-carbon conditions with wording favouring their joint application.
Deletes automotive industry from the sectors expressly identified in the recital on industrial requirements.

Adds a recital linking aluminium origin to electrolysis and first casting for primary production and relevant primary-input and scrap-casting operations for secondary production, excluding mere downstream processing.
Adds a recital supporting origin and low-carbon requirements for replacement rubber vehicle parts and procurement preference for truck and bus tyres retreaded in the EU.
Adds a recital arguing that only steel originally melted and poured in the EU should qualify as EU origin, including in components and assembled products, rather than downstream processing alone.
Adds a recital supporting predictable recycling of relevant ETS auction revenues into sectoral decarbonisation, matching demand measures with Innovation Fund and national investment support.
Adds plastics, including windows and pipes, to the methodology rationale and supports their inclusion in future ecodesign working plans and delegated acts.
Replaces reliance on implementing measures under construction-product and ecodesign legislation with requirements established in this Regulation itself.
Adds an express statement that EU-origin requirements should also be established alongside the low-carbon product approach.
Adds iron and plastics to the product groups addressed by the recital's low-carbon methodology provisions.
Adds flat glass to the construction materials addressed by the recital's low-carbon methodology provisions.
Replaces concrete with cement in the list of construction products whose low-carbon status is linked to existing product legislation.
Adds a recital restricting requirements to Annex II products and excluding otherwise uncovered systems where relevant accessory materials account for no more than 5% of total volume.
Adds a recital restricting requirements to Annex II products and excluding otherwise uncovered systems where relevant accessory materials account for no more than 5% of total volume.
Adds a recital restricting requirements to Annex II and III products and excluding otherwise uncovered systems where specified accessory materials do not exceed the applicable annex volume threshold.

Adds a recital supporting a technology-neutral sub-target for near-zero cement or binders within concrete and mortar requirements, covering carbon capture, clinker-free cement and alternative binders.
Adds a recital arguing that national electricity carbon intensity should not lead to discriminatory application of low-carbon criteria between producers.
Deletes the recital on lead markets, steel greenhouse-gas labelling, product-performance classes and the treatment of primary and secondary steel production.
Deletes the recital on lead markets, steel greenhouse-gas labelling, product-performance classes and the treatment of primary and secondary steel production.
Deletes the recital on lead markets, steel greenhouse-gas labelling, product-performance classes and the treatment of primary and secondary steel production.
Deletes the recital on lead markets, steel greenhouse-gas labelling, product-performance classes and the treatment of primary and secondary steel production.

Adds recognition of nuclear, low-carbon hydrogen and carbon-capture routes; EU-average electricity accounting with verified supply exceptions; separate import defaults; and safeguards against double counting or equating low-carbon status with EU origin.
Adds a transparent, comparable voluntary labelling and classification rationale, reusing ETS and CBAM data where possible to inform purchasing and investment choices.
Deletes the detailed rationale for performance classes that distinguish primary and secondary steel and reflect scrap content and climate-neutrality performance.

Strengthens the climate alignment of performance classes, explicitly distinguishing conventional from low-carbon routes and tying the top class to feasible near-zero production and verifiable reductions.

cat: EU-average energy mix in carbon accounting
txt: Adds that product greenhouse-gas intensity should use the EU-average energy mix to maintain equal treatment across Member States.
Deletes adjustment of emissions-intensity thresholds by scrap share for product categories typically requiring primary steel production.
Replaces effort-based and scrap-adjusted framing with full lifecycle assessment, resource efficiency and avoided emissions in steel performance classification.

cat: Mandatory rather than voluntary steel labelling
txt: Deletes the voluntary qualification attached to the labelling approach, removing the recital's express optionality.

Adds a recital supporting a common EU sector methodology while permitting compliant national methodologies reflecting energy systems and resources, subject to transparent, verifiable and non-discriminatory minimum standards.
Adds a recital supporting a common steel label, consistent calculation boundaries and scrap-sensitive performance classes, with the highest class aligned to EU climate neutrality.

Adds a recital linking rising concrete and mortar shares to construction-product rules, available standards and supply growth, recognising alternative binders, recycled inputs, efficiency, fuel switching and carbon capture.

cat: Legislative preparation of chemical demand measures
txt: Adds a recital calling for a chemical-sector work plan, studies and consultation, technology-neutral ISO-based carbon assessment and adoption of new demand measures through the ordinary legislative procedure.
Adds a recital calling for EU and national finance to accompany market creation and simplification, with merit-based EU allocations across strategic value chains and socioeconomic convergence.
Adds a recital calling for assessment of how EU law can support renewable and low-carbon refinery products and provide a viable case for large-scale decarbonisation investment.
Adds a recital calling for assessment of how EU law can support renewable and low-carbon refinery products and provide a viable case for large-scale decarbonisation investment.
Deletes the recital supporting minimum mandatory origin and low-carbon procurement specifications and explaining their application across contract types.
Adds a recital allowing multi-operator framework agreements to calibrate origin requirements across awards, provided at least 50% of their total value or volume complies.
Adds a recital allowing multi-operator framework agreements to calibrate origin requirements across awards, provided at least 50% of their total value or volume complies.

cat: Origin rules and minimum EU value added
txt: Adds a call to review Customs Code origin rules so last substantial transformation includes at least 50% EU added value, rather than low-value finishing of imported intermediates.

Adds a recital limiting requirements to covered public procurement and excluding critical electricity, gas or hydrogen network goods and works where application would jeopardise supply, reliability or timely delivery.
Adds a recital supporting exclusion of operators that fail to comply with applicable social and labour-law obligations.
Adds a recital supporting exclusion of operators that fail to comply with applicable social and labour-law obligations.
Replaces the recital's reference to EU customs legislation with a calculation based on the value of non-originating materials used in a product or component.
Adds EU-level criteria alongside mandatory technical specifications for origin and low-carbon requirements in public procurement.

Adds a recital allowing framework-agreement compliance where at least 50% of participating operators supply EU-origin products, rather than measuring compliance against total procurement value or volume.

Adds a recital allowing framework-agreement compliance where at least 50% of participating operators supply EU-origin products, rather than measuring compliance against total procurement value or volume.
Adds a recital calling for transition periods proportionate to industrial investment and supply-chain adaptation needs when origin or low-carbon requirements are introduced or tightened.
Adds a recital combining steel melt-and-pour origin, origin requirements for cement and clinker in concrete and mortar, and review of origin rules for all covered products and components.
Adds a recital supporting transition periods and continued eligibility throughout normal operational lifetimes for vehicles registered before new origin requirements apply.

cat: Limits on derogations and strategic dependencies
txt: Adds a recital restricting exemptions to objectively justified necessary cases and opposing lasting increases in strategic dependence or imported emissions.
Adds a recital supporting thresholds for steel, cement-related products and aluminium so small-value or small-quantity projects avoid disproportionate administrative burdens.
Adds a recital tying EU-origin steel, including steel in components and final products, to EU melt-and-pour operations and the existing traceability framework.
Adds a recital explaining that mixing imported cement should not suffice for EU origin and that concrete and mortar requirements must cover their cement and clinker inputs.

cat: Review and revision of origin rules
txt: Adds a recital calling for a product-specific origin assessment within 12 months and binding delegated rules within 18 months, including substantive aluminium production and recycling stages rather than mere remelting.
Deletes the recital justifying derogations where origin or low-carbon requirements are infeasible, excessively costly or restrictive of competition.
Strengthens the exceptional character of cost derogations and argues for 40% as a minimum protection threshold that the Commission may raise but not lower.
Adds technical incompatibility across projects, funding, regulatory frameworks and multi-year investment plans as grounds for derogation, particularly for utilities and State-owned enterprises.

cat: Product-level cost tests and project delays
txt: Adds comparison of the individual product price rather than total contract value, and derogations for major delays, threatened EU funding use or essential security interests.
Extends the incompatibility rationale to funding, regulatory and multi-year spending frameworks, recognising utilities' need for uninterrupted access to critical technologies.
Adds disproportionate costs, insufficient suitable supply, material implementation delays and significant competitive distortions to the cases justifying non-application of requirements.
Adds that decisions not to apply origin or low-carbon requirements should be justified by objective and transparent evidence.
Adds an express justification requirement to the recital's description of permissible procurement derogations.

cat: Public support coverage and relocation recovery
txt: Adds social and labour conditions, recovery after relocation within five years or three for SMEs, 90% budget coverage for specified household or business schemes and full coverage of other intervention and corporate-vehicle support.
Adds a recital linking support to origin, carbon and labour conditions and recovery if supported manufacturing relocates outside the EU within five years, or three years for SMEs.
Adds origin, carbon and labour conditions across construction, infrastructure, vehicle and other support, with recovery following relocation within five years or three for SMEs.

cat: Intangible EU value in origin calculations
txt: Adds a recital supporting inclusion of EU research, software, intellectual property and industrial transformation in component-value calculations, rather than relying solely on physical component geography.

Adds a recital supporting derogations where compliant supply is unavailable within reasonable delivery times and transport costs, and protection of ongoing cross-border infrastructure framework agreements.
Adds a recital calling for transition periods and continued use of vehicles registered before new origin requirements apply, avoiding retrospective eligibility restrictions.
Adds a recital calling for supported manufacturing to remain in the EU for five years, with recovery of aid plus nationally determined interest following relocation.

Adds a recital treating extra origin and low-carbon procurement costs as economic-security investment to be recognised when applying EU net-expenditure trajectories, including local and regional spending.
Adds a recital calling for appropriate transitions for new carbon or origin requirements to protect investment predictability and supply-chain continuity.
Deletes the recital explaining the automotive package's vehicle emissions credits, EU-made vehicles and associated origin requirements.

cat: Broader eligibility for vehicle emissions credits
txt: Broadens the recital's credit rationale beyond small affordable electric vehicles to zero- and low-emission vehicles, including vehicles exclusively using eligible fuels, and removes the original 2035-target description.

cat: Support for EU battery and vehicle production
txt: Adds a recital calling for EU or national incentives and output-based production support, including funding for EU battery components, alongside Annex III requirements.
Adds that automotive measures should recognise the full EU value chain and all technologies contributing to decarbonisation, rather than privileging a single propulsion route.

cat: Audited component valuation and origin tracing
txt: Adds a recital requiring comparable full-cost valuation for in-house and purchased parts, arm's-length group transactions and consistent tier-by-tier tracing, excluding profits, general overheads and non-EU research from EU value.

cat: EU research bonus for vehicle compliance
txt: Adds a recital supporting a fleet-compliance bonus for manufacturers concentrating research and development in the EU, to retain vehicle technology, intellectual property, skills and employment.
Adds a recital opposing stranded zero-emission buses and coaches or disrupted investment caused by new origin requirements, especially in smaller and peripheral markets.
Adds a recital calling for vehicle-origin implementation to reflect availability and operational needs so public transport remains continuous and affordable, including in peripheral or small markets.
Adds acceptance of existing invoices, delivery notes and supplier statements and long-term supplier declarations, reducing documentation created solely to prove origin compliance.
Adds support for one self-declaration or equivalent document and reuse of existing evidence, opposing duplicate applications or documentation unless verification objectively requires them.
Rejects reliance solely on operator declarations and adds access to production, customs, tax, labour and supply-chain evidence and, where appropriate, independent verification or audit.
Deletes the specific recital requirement for manufacturers to indicate origin compliance when issuing the vehicle certificate of conformity.
Adds regular ex-post verification and remedies following a final finding of non-compliance, including procurement exclusion, contract termination or other available measures.

cat: Risk-based verification and reusable vehicle documents
txt: Adds that further evidence and checks should be risk-based and vehicle compliance documents harmonised and reusable across procurement, public support and corporate-vehicle measures.
Adds reduced SME regulatory and administrative burdens and assessment of appropriate de minimis procurement award thresholds.
Replaces the self-declaration emphasis with safeguards against weaker environmental obligations, early consultation, brownfield mapping and coordination, and properly resourced public authorities.
Adds express attention to SMEs in the recital's approach to proportionate compliance verification and administrative burden.

Adds a recital allowing compliant and potentially exempt services in one procurement procedure, but restricting awards to non-compliant alternatives to cases lacking suitable compliant bids or meeting exemption conditions.
Adds prior assessment and sector consultation addressing EU capacity, supply, costs, downstream users, SMEs and bottlenecks, together with transition periods.
Adds that origin requirements should not be reduced without justification and demonstrated EU supply or production insufficiency, preserving investment predictability.
Adds periodic monitoring communicated to Parliament and consideration of recommendations from Member States and Parliament when requirements are reassessed.

cat: Legislative review instead of delegated revision
txt: Replaces Commission power to revise requirements with monitoring and, where appropriate, a legislative proposal supported by assessment of national, household, SME and budget effects.

cat: Ordinary legislative procedure for substantive changes
txt: Adds regular monitoring and requires substantive changes to origin or carbon requirements to follow a Commission proposal, impact assessment and the ordinary legislative procedure.
Adds global conditions and international trade and investment flows to the factors relevant to reviewing industrial requirements.
Adds that the Commission should consider the relevant revision factors within an impact assessment.
Reorients the review criteria towards available and affordable products and inputs, diversified resilient supply chains, industrial competitiveness and changing trade conditions.
Replaces the alternatives permitting either type of requirement or both with wording favouring joint origin and low-carbon requirements in revisions.

Adds a recital calling for a consulted work plan, end-product coverage to prevent downstream circumvention and tailored origin, carbon and sustainable-carbon measures, with delegated action confined to procurement and support schemes.

cat: EU sourcing of battery raw materials
txt: Adds a recital supporting a technology-neutral requirement for at least 20% by mass of relevant strategic battery raw materials to be mined, processed or recycled in the EU.
Adds a recital supporting Commission extension of strategic sectors against objective criteria and consultation, covering complete productive ecosystems rather than final assembly alone.
Adds a recital supporting delegated extension of lead-market requirements to further energy-intensive products, combining ecodesign carbon rules with EU-origin conditions to retain production.

cat: Sunset and review of origin requirements
txt: Adds a recital treating origin requirements as a last-resort, temporary response to capability gaps, with regular review and expiry unless the co-legislators extend them.
Adds a recital supporting delegated acts for procurement and public-intervention demand measures promoting EU low-carbon chemicals and sustainable-carbon-source products.
Adds a recital opposing retroactive application to earlier investments, ownership and technology structures, supplier contracts and previously approved expansions.

Adds a recital supporting a dedicated fertiliser work plan based on studies, socioeconomic assessment and stakeholder consultation, aligned with verified carbon labelling and relevant agricultural value chains.

cat: Legislation for demand measures beyond public support
txt: Adds a recital requiring demonstrated need, careful assessment and sector consultation before extending demand measures beyond public procurement and intervention through dedicated legislative packages.

Adds a recital supporting vessel-wide EU-content shares and sourcing requirements for strategic maritime equipment, based on sector-specific assessment, common nomenclature, regular review and structured consultation.
Adds emphasis on non-EU investment and local workforce use and medium- and long-term professional training within the investment contribution rationale.
Extends the recital's investment framing to net-zero technologies and investments made through foreign-owned subsidiaries, rather than only directly by foreign investors.

Adds risks from third-country dependencies and extends the rationale to controlled subsidiaries and established strategic activities, broadening the proposed investment framework beyond emerging sectors.
Adds research and development, employment and skills to the forms of EU value creation expected from covered foreign investment, with an appropriateness qualification.
Deletes the statement that Member State investment conditions fragment the internal market by creating unequal conditions for investors.
Adds a recital supporting application of foreign-investment conditions from publication of the 5 March 2025 automotive action plan, to prevent projects accelerating before the new rules apply.
Broadens investment coverage to threatened existing capacity and additional net-zero and critical-material sectors, including relevant foreign subsidiaries and objective scope criteria.
Adds reliance on beneficial ownership to capture indirect holding chains, EU or third-country intermediate companies and State-owned investors.

cat: Lower concentration threshold and net-zero scope
txt: Lowers the relevant third-country global-capacity threshold from 40% to 20%, adds net-zero technologies and subsidiaries, and presents that lower share as capable of generating strategic dependence.
Adds safeguards against unnecessary duplication or conflicts with national and EU law and undue administrative burdens in the investment framework.
Clarifies that the global-capacity test follows the investment's ultimate owner or controller, including nationality where that controller is an individual.
Extends the rationale to associated strategic industrial activities and preservation or reinforcement of existing EU manufacturing capabilities, rather than only building new capacity.
Adds net-zero technologies and investments by foreign subsidiaries to the sectors and investment routes described in the recital.
Reduces the third-country share of global sectoral manufacturing capacity relevant to investment conditions from 40% to 20%.
Extends the rationale to established and net-zero sectors and indirect investment, and lowers the relevant global manufacturing-capacity threshold from 40% to 30%.
Adds a recital supporting onshore and offshore wind coverage under Chapter IV to retain manufacturing, skills and supply chains and avoid new dependencies.
Adds a recital supporting foreign-investment coverage for semiconductors, digital technologies, AI and quantum activities to retain production, knowledge, skills and supply security.
Adds prioritisation of disused industrial land to prevent deterioration and unmanaged pollution while returning sites to productive economic use.
Adds an explicit distinction between new-site investment and acquisition, modernisation, expansion, conversion or reopening of existing productive assets.

cat: Emerging and established strategic investment sectors
txt: Adds a recital recognising batteries, electric and fuel-cell vehicles, solar and hydrogen technologies alongside established wind manufacturing as requiring particular investment scrutiny and retained EU capabilities.

Adds a recital aligning notification and assessment with the foreign-investment screening framework, reusing authorities, information and timelines while maintaining distinct industrial-value and security assessments.
Adds reliance on existing national investment-screening authorities and procedures and respect for national institutional arrangements and allocation of competences.
Extends the recital beyond emerging sectors to established strategic and net-zero sectors and updates its investment-screening legislative references.
Deletes the 'emerging' qualification, broadening the stated investment rationale to strategic sectors that are already established.
Adds net-zero technologies to the strategic-sector investment rationale.

Broadens the protected interests to employment, skills, strategic assets and established sectors, supports proportionate conditions on controlled intermediary entities and recasts Commission involvement as a non-binding opinion.
Adds net-zero technologies and strengthens application of conditions to foreign subsidiaries, removing qualifications based on alternative measures and the Commission's proportionality intervention.
Removes the emerging-sector qualification and the limitation tying criteria to clearly necessary security, supply and environmental protection, supporting wider application to covered investments.

cat: Foreign shareholding limits and workforce conditions
txt: Adds compliance conditions and limits on third-country company shareholdings to prevent dominant positions in the European market.
Deletes the proportionality safeguard allowing Commission intervention concerning conditions imposed on investments through foreign subsidiaries.
Adds an express requirement that subsidiary-related conditions rest on a case-by-case risk assessment and the principle of proportionality.

cat: Indirect ownership and equal investment obligations
txt: Adds equivalent notification and substantive conditions for subsidiaries and looks through free-trade-agreement-country entities to qualifying third-country beneficial owners to prevent circumvention.
Adds consideration of cumulative ownership concentration from successive acquisitions and significant holdings across competitors or value chains, even where individual stakes do not confer control.
Adds consideration of sustainable recovery, retained production and employment, skills and local industrial regeneration when restructuring changes beneficial ownership or control.
Extends the recital's treatment of investment and restructuring operations to foreign investors' subsidiaries as well as direct investors.

Adds a recital calling for scrutiny of acquisition debt, holding horizons, distributions and asset sales, distinguishing credible industrial investment from short-term financial strategies that weaken productive capacity and employment.
Adds a recital excluding investments made before entry into force from new contribution conditions while preserving application to qualifying new investments.

Adds a recital recognising public investment funds as potential long-term capital providers while supporting enhanced scrutiny of concerning third-country influence, governance, financing and strategic objectives.
Lowers the investment threshold from EUR 100 million to EUR 33 million and expands the rationale to established, critical and net-zero sectors and areas of lost or insufficient EU production.
Lowers the investment threshold from EUR 100 million to EUR 50 million and expressly includes net-zero technologies in the sectoral rationale.
Lowers the investment threshold from EUR 100 million to EUR 30 million and adds potential effects on SMEs to the justification for scrutiny.
Reduces the investment value threshold described in the recital from EUR 100 million to EUR 50 million, bringing smaller investments within the stated rationale.
Reduces the investment value threshold described in the recital from EUR 100 million to EUR 50 million, bringing smaller investments within the stated rationale.
Reduces the investment value threshold described in the recital from EUR 100 million to EUR 50 million, bringing smaller investments within the stated rationale.
Reduces the investment value threshold described in the recital from EUR 100 million to EUR 50 million, bringing smaller investments within the stated rationale.
Lowers the investment threshold from EUR 100 million to EUR 50 million and removes the emerging-sector qualification.
Adds coordination allowing screening and industrial-value assessments to proceed in parallel under this Regulation and the foreign-investment screening framework.
Adds independence and suitably trained, experienced staff to the institutional requirements described for investment assessment.
Adds express flexibility for Member States to rely on existing competent authorities and administrative structures.
Adds established and net-zero sectors to the institutional rationale and links assessment to the updated foreign-investment screening Regulation.
Adds investments through subsidiaries and deletes the emerging-sector limitation in the recital on national investment authorities.
Adds that notification concerns investors from third countries holding over 40% of global capacity in the relevant emerging strategic sector and investing in that field within the EU.
Adds prevention of monopolies that could harm the internal market over the medium and long term to the investment-notification rationale.

cat: Lower notification threshold and subsidiary coverage
txt: Lowers the ownership or control notification threshold from 30% to 10% and expressly includes foreign investors' subsidiaries.

cat: Lower notification threshold and subsidiary coverage
txt: Lowers the ownership or control notification threshold from 30% to 10% and expressly includes foreign investors' subsidiaries.
Reduces the ownership or control notification threshold from 30% to 20%.
Reduces the ownership or control notification threshold from 30% to 15%.
Adds subsidiaries and expressly opposes splitting a single economic operation between investors, vehicles or transactions to avoid investment or notification thresholds.
Adds that the relevant aggregated notification threshold should not exceed an EU-established share, favouring a common ceiling rather than unconstrained threshold setting.
Adds subsidiaries to the investors whose related holdings and investments should be aggregated to prevent threshold avoidance.
Adds subsidiaries and supports proportionate national golden-share, pre-emption, authorisation and targeted veto arrangements to protect strategic assets, technology and productive capacity.
Clarifies that foreign ownership and control limits apply to investors acting alone or jointly, both at the outset and throughout subsequent development of the investment.
Adds that foreign ownership and control limits should apply where necessary and proportionate to the investment's risks and EU value contribution.
Adds foreign subsidiaries to the recital's ownership and control restrictions, extending its look-through approach beyond direct investors.
Adds that joint-venture requirements should be necessary and proportionate to the risks and EU value contribution of the investment.
Extends the joint-venture rationale to net-zero and established sectors and investments made by foreign subsidiaries.
Adds foreign subsidiaries to the recital's joint-venture and ownership participation conditions.

cat: Lawful technology licensing and know-how transfer
txt: Adds that licensing and know-how transfers must comply with intellectual-property, competition, confidentiality and economic-security rules.
Changes encouragement of technology or know-how contributions into a requirement and extends the recital to foreign subsidiaries.

cat: Retention and use of EU intellectual property
txt: Adds safeguards preserving EU targets' rights to develop and exploit results and opposing transfers or exclusive licences placing strategic intangible assets under exclusive third-country control.
Adds subsidiaries and opposes transferring pre-existing, independently developed or subsequent intellectual property outside the EU without Investment Authority or Commission authorisation.
Adds explicit compliance with EU intellectual-property, competition, confidentiality, data-protection and economic-security rules.
Adds foreign investors' subsidiaries to the recital's intellectual-property ownership and related technology arrangements.
Adds a recital supporting authority approval before transferring relevant pre-existing, independently developed or subsequent intellectual-property rights and assets outside the EU.

Recasts research contributions around sustained EU research, engineering and industrialisation capabilities, cooperation with universities and clusters and retention of skilled personnel, including for subsidiary investments.

cat: Employment and skills contributions from investment
txt: Adds that foreign investment should create employment and finance education and training supporting EU industrial and technological development.
Adds implementation of innovative solutions and medium- and long-term development of the specialised workforce needed to meet EU objectives.
Adds foreign subsidiaries to the recital's research and development contribution expectations.
Deletes the recital supporting EU-worker participation, training and application of workforce thresholds across occupational categories.

cat: Majority EU workforce and regional skills
txt: Adds a majority EU-workforce emphasis and stronger training, reskilling and local partnership considerations, especially for industrial regions undergoing restructuring or technological change.

Adds annual full-time-equivalent calculation of the 50% threshold across the workforce, separate tests for research categories, and exclusion of artificial recruitment arrangements used to meet the threshold.
Adds a 75% EU-workforce ambition at each site, counting agency and subcontracted workers, together with decent conditions, collective-agreement compliance and foreign-subsidiary coverage.
Adds a 60% EU-workforce ambition at each site, decent working conditions and collective-agreement safeguards, and coverage of net-zero activities and foreign subsidiaries.
Deletes the requirement to meet workforce thresholds separately across operational, technical, supervisory and managerial categories.

cat: EU workforce thresholds and lawful residents
txt: Adds a 50% EU-worker baseline and 66% for publicly supported investment within three years of production, limited commissioning flexibility and inclusion of legally resident, authorised third-country workers.

cat: Domestic value creation and supply diversification
txt: Adds EU value added, longer-term skills and technology capabilities and more resilient, diversified strategic supply chains to the sourcing rationale.
Adds consideration of actual EU availability, technical and quality specifications, foundry components and avoidance of strategic supply-chain disruption when applying sourcing expectations.

cat: 30% EU sourcing and substantive investment benefits
txt: Specifies at least 30% EU inputs and emphasises avoiding mere assembly factories while securing lasting economic and employment value.

cat: Broader sectors and meaningful EU sourcing
txt: Extends sourcing expectations to net-zero and established sectors and strengthens the reference to a substantial EU input share defined by the Regulation.
