Adds coordination enabling investment screening and industrial contribution assessments to proceed in parallel under the foreign-investment screening framework.

Replaces the four-of-six approach with mandatory EU ownership, joint-venture and employment conditions plus a technological contribution through intellectual property, know-how or EU research activity.
Removes the 'at least four of six' qualification and adds foreign subsidiaries, strengthening the recital's expectation that the investment conditions apply as a full set.
Deletes the four-of-six choice and adds foreign subsidiaries to the recital's approval and compliance framework.
Adds the qualifier 'national' to references to Investment Authorities, clarifying the administrative level responsible for assessment and decisions.
Replaces the four-of-six approach with all six conditions and extends the recital to foreign subsidiaries.
Replaces fulfilment of at least four out of six conditions with at least two out of four, reducing the compliance combination described in the recital.
Replaces the minimum four-of-six approach with fulfilment of all investment conditions.
Deletes the four-of-six qualification, leaving the recital to refer to the conditions as a whole rather than a selectable subset.

cat: Optional Commission involvement in investment review
txt: Limits notification to the Commission to relevant cases where a Member State seeks assessment of scope, compliance and approval, rather than general Commission monitoring of all notifications.
Adds that Member States should communicate received investment notifications to the Commission in a timely manner.
Replaces wording that Member States should inform the Commission with wording that they may do so, weakening the recital's expectation of systematic information sharing.
Deletes the recital supporting Commission opinions on how investment conditions apply and explaining Member States' response to those opinions.

cat: National discretion and non-binding Commission opinions
txt: Emphasises national investment-control competence, expands protected industrial and environmental interests and makes Commission opinions non-binding, removing publicity, timing and justification elements of the original approach.

cat: Shared opinions and stronger Member State explanations
txt: Adds sharing of Commission opinions with all Investment Authorities, refers to six mandatory conditions and strengthens expectations for explanations and justifications of national decisions.

cat: Commission opinion sharing and national justification
txt: Adds sharing of the Commission opinion with the relevant Member State's Investment Authority and strengthens the wording requiring that State to justify its treatment of the opinion.
Deletes the recital supporting Commission review of investments affecting the internal market or EU supply chains.
Deletes the recital supporting Commission review of investments affecting the internal market or EU supply chains.

cat: Commission review and critical raw materials
txt: Adds critical raw-material investments and empowers the Commission to prescribe application of conditions to the national Investment Authority.
Conditions Commission review on a likely significant impact and adds EU security and economic resilience to the grounds for intervention.
Deletes the reference to Commission action on its own initiative, narrowing the stated routes through which EU-level investment review may be triggered.
Removes 'be able to', strengthening the recital's wording concerning Commission review rather than describing it only as an available possibility.

cat: Protection of existing net-zero technology leadership
txt: Adds a recital supporting national conditions, including proportionate refusal of investment, to prevent foreign subsidies and market distortions undermining EU leadership in established net-zero technologies.
Adds a recital supporting the same investment conditions for critical raw-material exploration as for extraction, processing and recycling, preventing vulnerabilities at the start of the value chain.

cat: Protection of existing net-zero technology leadership
txt: Adds a recital supporting conditions, including refusal, on investment in net-zero technologies where distortive foreign practices could create future quasi-monopolies and supply-chain disruption.
Adds a medium- and long-term perspective to monitoring whether foreign-investment benefits are retained within the internal market.
Specifies national Investment Authorities as responsible for monitoring continuing compliance during operation of the investment.
Deletes 'as appropriate', strengthening the expectation that investment conditions are monitored throughout operation rather than only selectively.

cat: Broader monitoring of global investment risks
txt: Adds international trade and investment flows and technological change, with attention to chokepoints, supply concentration, distortions, shortages and overcapacity, while removing the emerging-sector limitation.

Adds review of thresholds and conditions and requires extension of investment coverage through an assessed legislative proposal under the ordinary legislative procedure rather than Commission implementing action.
Adds proportionality to the principles relevant to monitoring and adjusting investment measures.
Adds local authorities, social and social-economy actors, grid resilience, existing skills and research evidence to designation, linking industrial areas to quality jobs and durable local value.
Adds neighbouring Member State cooperation, priority for integrated clusters and an overarching framework bringing existing acceleration valleys and strategic projects together without duplication.

Adds transport and energy infrastructure, affordable clean energy, specialist skills, shared research facilities and cooperation between firms, researchers and authorities as foundations for industrial areas.
Adds treatment of acceleration areas as coordinated investment ecosystems and facilitated access to EU finance for qualifying industrial, innovation, decarbonisation and resilience projects.
Adds recognition of existing clusters and sites suitable for modernisation, expansion, repurposing or decarbonisation, including joint energy-intensive and clean-technology projects.
Adds reliance on existing valley information, assessments and plans when designating acceleration areas, reducing administrative duplication while addressing any additional requirements.
Adds local and outermost-region considerations and energy-system safeguards, opposing transfer of project costs to citizens and supporting compensation where household energy costs rise.

cat: Coal regions and closed industrial sites
txt: Adds coal and carbon-intensive just-transition regions and supports inclusion of existing installations and closed or closing mines and power stations in acceleration areas.

cat: Voluntary and nationally adapted area designation
txt: Recasts designation around a demonstrated industrial case and constitutional and regional arrangements, recognising existing clusters and brownfields instead of requiring narrowly bounded new areas.
Adds local-level cooperation and energy-infrastructure safeguards so industrial-area demand does not compromise other network users.
Adds that the industrial-area provision should not restrict access to public funding.
Makes acceleration-area development voluntary, removes the limited-geographical-scope rationale and strengthens references to close local and regional cooperation.
Recasts designation as an option compatible with national industrial, energy and spatial-planning priorities, emphasising strategic investment and industrial cooperation.

cat: Industrial symbiosis and shared resource flows
txt: Adds a recital supporting exchange of heat, cold, hydrogen, CO2, water, by-products and secondary materials between industrial installations to improve resource efficiency and reduce emissions.

cat: Automatic recognition of existing acceleration valleys
txt: Adds a recital deeming previously designated Net-Zero Acceleration Valleys to be industrial acceleration areas while they meet the relevant criteria, without changing their existing obligations.

Adds a recital supporting designation of ports, including small and medium-sized ports, for maritime, renewable-energy, defence and specialised manufacturing activities linked to local skills and hinterland infrastructure.

Adds a recital allowing diverse industrial, SME, research and innovation participants and non-contiguous sites linked by coordinated investment or integrated value chains, reflecting local territorial conditions.
Adds a recital excluding Natura 2000 and other protected or sensitive areas from acceleration-area boundaries and requiring attention to climate risks and water protection.
Adds a recital supporting regional, local and stakeholder involvement in identification, designation and governance of acceleration areas to improve territorial integration and public support.
Adds a recital prioritising energy-intensive decarbonisation and resource-efficient production, including repair, reuse, remanufacturing and recycling.
Adds a recital calling for area designation to protect ecosystems and biodiversity and deliver benefits to nearby communities, citizens and workers.

Adds a recital supporting tax, infrastructure and restoration contributions by companies and safeguards against local revenue loss and environmental damage associated with extractive or fly-in/fly-out operations.
Adds a recital linking industrial areas to renewable acceleration areas, circularity hubs and industrial symbiosis to improve electricity access and regional secondary-material loops.
Adds a recital identifying road, rail, ports, intermodal terminals, last-mile access, rest facilities and goods-transport energy infrastructure as relevant to area designation.
Adds a recital calling on Member States with outermost regions to designate at least one industrial acceleration area there, reflecting higher costs and structural constraints.

cat: Coordination of innovation and industrial finance
txt: Adds links to EU competitiveness, research, STEP, critical-material, chips, net-zero and common-interest instruments, supporting a continuum from research through demonstration to scaled industrial production.
Adds coordinated project pipelines and funding guidance where areas overlap with Net-Zero Acceleration Valleys, reusing support structures while respecting programme eligibility and State aid rules.
Adds renewable acceleration areas to the EU frameworks with which industrial area development should be coordinated.
Adds renewable acceleration areas to the EU frameworks with which industrial area development should be coordinated.

Adds a recital supporting grid electricity for hydrogen produced and used within acceleration areas without renewable-hydrogen additionality or temporal and geographical correlation requirements, while retaining support eligibility.

Adds collection, preparation and recycling of European material streams as complements to extraction and refining, supporting EU reintegration of recovered strategic materials and reduced imported emissions.
Adds that participation in the critical-material joint-purchasing mechanism should be voluntary and used where appropriate.
Deletes the reference to small mid-caps in the recital describing firms benefiting from joint strategic raw-material purchasing.

Adds long-term, cost-reflective industrial energy arrangements linked to nuclear or hydroelectric assets, coordinated grid planning and protection against wholesale-price volatility eroding their competitive advantage.
Calls for a comprehensive technology-neutral analysis and removes the requirement for a separate assessment for every area and the specified link to national grid planning.

cat: Prior infrastructure assessment and workforce access
txt: Adds assessment before major investment and attention to roads, product movements and transport access for workers living outside the immediate area.

cat: Prior designation assessment and network coordination
txt: Adds assessment before area designation in cooperation with system operators and expressly covers digital, electricity, gas and hydrogen infrastructure.

cat: Timely access to multiple infrastructure networks
txt: Strengthens the emphasis on timely connections and adds pipeline, digital, hydrogen and electricity infrastructure rather than referring only to faster energy connections.
Replaces the timely-energy wording with reliable, secure and competitively priced energy as the relevant enabling condition.

Adds a recital linking demand measures to affordable energy, raw materials, infrastructure and stable regulation, respecting national energy mixes and recognising renewables, nuclear, biomass, storage and efficiency.

cat: Low-carbon energy assets within acceleration areas
txt: Adds a recital treating necessary low-carbon energy infrastructure, including modular reactors, geothermal, industrial heating and cooling, cogeneration, storage and connections, as integral to the accelerated industrial area.
Adds a recital requiring area planning to anticipate lifetime climate risks and assess water availability alongside household, agricultural and ecosystem needs.

cat: Skills and training in acceleration areas
txt: Deletes the recital linking area designation to access to education, training and relevant industrial skills.

cat: STEM education and regional skills ecosystems
txt: Adds apprenticeships, reskilling and youth access, territorial STEM strategies and partnerships between firms, schools, universities and training bodies, linking acceleration areas to durable industrial skills and innovative SMEs.
Adds integrated ecosystems attractive to workers and innovative firms, supporting decarbonised production, circular business models and processing, recovery and retention of critical raw materials.
Adds access to vocational education and training, including adequate specialist funding, as necessary for skilled labour and the industrial impact of acceleration areas.
Adds a medium- and long-term specialist vocational-training perspective to the skills provision for industrial areas.
Adds respect for constitutional competences and coordinated national, regional and local action, retaining installation-specific permits with their authorities while seeking a common timetable.

cat: Coverage and transparency of baseline permits
txt: Adds all strategic and operational infrastructure projects to the baseline-permit rationale and calls for an explicit list of covered and separately required permits.
Adds that accelerated industrial areas must not slow other projects' permits and links designation to digitalisation and procedural efficiencies.
Adds that baseline permits for areas on existing industrial sites may integrate, update or consolidate existing authorisations where appropriate.

cat: Expected administrative benefits of baseline permits
txt: Deletes the stronger claim that baseline permits will significantly accelerate procedures and reduce administrative burdens, retaining the broader permitting arrangement.
Deletes 'where required' from the reference to environmental assessments still needed beyond the baseline permit, removing that qualification from the recital.

Adds a recital recognising remote territories' supply and infrastructure constraints and supporting adapted origin requirements where compliance creates disproportionate costs or delays, while favouring local production.
Deletes the recital justifying delegated Commission powers over equivalence, product requirements, demand measures and investment rules.
Restricts delegated powers to defined non-essential technical elements and reserves substantive origin, carbon or scope changes to assessed proposals under the ordinary legislative procedure.

Adds pharmaceuticals and maritime industries to delegated demand-measure powers and reframes product-list and requirement powers around enhancement rather than the original third-country exclusion list.
Adds zero-emission vessels and maritime equipment and delegated specification of category-specific procurement and support cost-difference rules, alongside net-zero technology coverage.
Adds vessels and maritime equipment and category-specific cost-difference rules to the matters for which Commission delegated powers are envisaged.

cat: Category-specific cost rules and net-zero coverage
txt: Adds delegated specification and differentiation of procurement and support cost-difference rules for covered categories and net-zero technologies.
Deletes the third-country non-equivalence list from the matters expressly delegated to the Commission in the recital.

cat: Institutional control over scope and equivalence
txt: Reserves wider obligations to the ordinary legislative procedure, favours Member State-controlled implementing acts for equivalence decisions and limits technical carbon methodology powers to the Regulation's principles.
Adds express assessment of relevant effects within impact assessments supporting the Commission's exercise of powers.
Deletes the specific reference to taking Critical Chemicals Alliance recommendations into account when developing chemical demand measures.
Deletes the specific reference to taking Critical Chemicals Alliance recommendations into account when developing chemical demand measures.
Recasts delegated powers as granting, reviewing, suspending or withdrawing third-country equivalent-origin treatment rather than simply changing a non-equivalence list.
Adds a recital seeking favourable application to association and trade partners, customs-union and EEA countries, avoiding unjustified disadvantages to those already integrated in EU value chains.

Adds a recital supporting Commission demand and content measures in sectoral crises involving lost market share, viability, competitiveness or rising emissions, favouring EU sustainable and low-carbon production.
Adds a recital supporting maintenance, restart, modernisation, expansion and decarbonisation of EU chemical capacity to reduce strategic dependencies.
Adds a recital supporting use of Better Regulation tools and the Committee of the Regions' RegHub network to identify administrative burdens, territorial effects and implementation obstacles.

cat: Limits and scope of implementing powers
txt: Adds templates, third-country exclusion and updated investment-condition references, while opposing implementing acts changing essential elements such as thresholds, emissions methodologies or criteria weighting.
Replaces the implementing-power approach with Article 290 delegated acts for origin calculations, standard templates and verification, explicitly excluding changes to essential elements.
Adds employment, skills, workforce retention, manufacturing capacity, market share and greenhouse-gas intensity of energy-intensive and net-zero sectors to the Commission's evaluation basis.
Adds employment, skills, workforce retention, manufacturing capacity, market share and greenhouse-gas intensity of energy-intensive and net-zero sectors to the Commission's evaluation basis.
Adds Commission guidelines, where appropriate, to support uniform implementation of penalties across Member States.

Limits penalties to direct operator obligations, allows existing enforcement regimes, opposes duplicate sanctions and protects reasonable reliance on valid supplier evidence, without excluding corrective or recovery measures.
Adds a recital calling for comprehensive sectoral assessment of economic, social and administrative effects, including competitiveness, investment, compliance costs and SMEs.
Deletes the recital supporting review of Chapters III and IV and consideration of additional sectoral measures and investment scrutiny.

Recasts review around comprehensive impact assessment, including plastics, flat glass and foundries, and supports an amending legislative proposal only where broader coverage is justified and proportionate.

Adds rail infrastructure, aerospace, robotics, biotech, quantum, defence, technical textiles, fertilisers, bioeconomy, construction and machinery to potential review coverage, extending beyond the original transport examples.

Adds rail manufacturing and infrastructure, aerospace, robotics, fertilisers, bioeconomy, construction materials and machinery and consideration of wider strategic and energy-intensive sector coverage.
Adds the chemical industry's strategic value-chain role, energy and emissions intensity, pollution impacts and circular low-carbon potential to the sectors to examine in review.

cat: EU value retention and technical-textile review
txt: Adds review of stronger EU value-added and critical-component retention thresholds and coverage of technical textiles for critical applications.
Adds technical textiles for defence, aerospace, healthcare, transport, personal protection and critical infrastructure to the sectors considered for broader coverage.
Replaces the narrower construction reference with rail manufacturing and infrastructure construction and operation, expressly including track, signalling and sensor technologies.
Replaces consideration of enhanced investment review with a rationale for applying Chapter IV requirements to zero-emission and hybrid aircraft, including unmanned systems.
Adds Annex II minimum low-carbon and EU-origin shares for energy-intensive industries to the matters assessed during review.
Adds chemical production, particularly fertilisers, to the sectors considered for broader measures during review.

Adds a recital supporting dissuasive, worldwide-turnover-linked fines for intentionally or grossly negligently false, inaccurate or misleading compliance declarations, to remove the incentive to misrepresent origin.
Adds that permitting digitalisation should avoid extra burdens and protect personal data, trade secrets, sensitive industrial information and cybersecurity.
Adds critical scale and production capacity for emissions reduction, energy efficiency and resource efficiency to the rationale for amending the Net-Zero Industry Act.
Adds proportionality, technology neutrality and contribution to manufacturing capacity and competitiveness to the net-zero legislative rationale.

Adds a recital supporting value-chain-specific origin rules, whole-project assessment for complex nuclear projects, phased requirements where EU supply is limited and long-term investment signals, including from 2035.

cat: Updating technology coverage for nuclear programmes
txt: Adds regular updates to covered technology and component lists, including needs of Member States developing or expanding nuclear energy programmes.
Adds an exclusion for electricity-generation contracts that receive no public support, auction award or other public intervention.
Adds transport charging technologies and electricity-grid technologies to the net-zero procurement coverage described in the recital.
Adds the option of holistic 'Made in EU' criteria for certain technologies rather than relying solely on individual component-origin requirements.
Adds geothermal and electricity-grid technologies to the procurement-origin rationale.
Adds solar-thermal and electric-charging technologies to the procurement-origin rationale.
Adds solar thermal, charging and grid technologies while deleting nuclear-fission energy technologies from the list.
Deletes the recital's express reliance on operator self-declaration for compliance with net-zero procurement requirements.
Adds electricity-grid technologies to the technologies addressed by additional EU-origin procurement requirements.
Adds electricity-grid technologies to the technologies addressed by additional EU-origin procurement requirements.
Adds electricity-grid technologies to the technologies addressed by additional EU-origin procurement requirements.
Adds solar-thermal technologies to the technologies addressed by additional EU-origin procurement requirements.
Deletes nuclear-fission energy technologies from the recital's list of technologies facing additional origin procurement requirements.
Replaces onshore and offshore wind technologies with semiconductors and strengthens the expected EU share from an unspecified proportion to a majority.

Adds a recital supporting phased grid requirements, starting with active digital and control systems and offshore-substation assembly, then passive equipment as EU capacity expands, to protect security and avoid token compliance.
Adds a recital calling for urgent resilience-list updates to include wind converters, electrolyser rectifiers and additional wind components such as flange foundations and bearing rings.
Adds a recital recognising grid digitalisation and new electricity demand and calling for additional grid components in the Net-Zero Industry Act framework and resilience implementing rules.
Adds a recital linking electrification-driven demand to EU grid manufacturing and seeking urgent inclusion of additional grid components in the applicable net-zero and resilience lists.
Adds low-carbon technologies to the recital describing the clarified scope of Net-Zero Industry Act procurement rules.

cat: Low-carbon, nuclear and geothermal auction coverage
txt: Broadens the recital's auction rationale to low-carbon technologies and adds nuclear fusion, nuclear fission and geothermal technologies.
Adds solar-thermal technologies to the technologies addressed by auction-related EU-origin requirements.
Replaces the renewable-only wording with net-zero and low-carbon energy technologies in the rationale for stricter auction coverage and opt-out conditions.

Adds a recital arguing that temporary EU production premiums should not alone trigger opt-outs and that cost assessment should consider lifecycle costs, security, resilience, strategic dependencies and cybersecurity.

Adds a recital supporting delegated specification of technology-specific cost-difference rules for net-zero procurement and auctions, reflecting sector characteristics and avoiding unnecessary burdens.

Adds a recital supporting delegated specification of technology-specific cost-difference rules for net-zero procurement and auctions, reflecting sector characteristics and avoiding unnecessary burdens.

cat: Battery precursors, active materials and circularity
txt: Adds a recital supporting origin requirements for battery precursors and active materials and retention and recycling of end-of-life batteries within the EU to secure strategic inputs.
Adds a recital supporting a minimum 20% EU-extracted, processed or recycled lithium share in batteries to stimulate EU projects and reduce external dependence.

cat: Grid security and phased origin requirements
txt: Adds a recital supporting origin requirements across grid procurement, auctions and support schemes, addressing concentrated suppliers and remote-control risks while providing phased implementation and shortage safeguards.

Adds low-carbon coverage, favours support bonuses over automatic eligibility exclusion where appropriate, removes the maximum-aid-intensity sentence and prioritises product availability and protection against increased energy poverty or delayed access.
Adds flexibility not to apply origin requirements to schemes targeting vulnerable households or energy and transport poverty, protecting price and product choice.
Recasts the support-scheme rationale around certain net-zero and low-carbon technologies rather than the original specific battery, photovoltaic and heat-pump list and green-transition wording.
Adds that all existing support schemes should comply with the Net-Zero Industry Act Annex II requirements by 2030.
Adds an exemption from EU-origin requirements where financial support consists exclusively of promotional loans or guarantees.
Adds transport charging technologies and electricity-grid technologies to the support-scheme origin coverage.
Adds solar-thermal technologies to the support-scheme origin coverage.

Adds a recital supporting extension to large private non-residential building and infrastructure works of at least 10,000 m² from 1 January 2032, broadening demand beyond public purchasing and support.
Adds a recital linking the Regulation to a broader industrial strategy and coordinated EU funding, including the European Competitiveness Fund, to mobilise public and private investment.

cat: SME access to strategic value chains
txt: Adds a recital applying 'Think Small First', reduced administrative burdens and easier finance and participation for smaller firms in strategic projects and industrial innovation.
Adds a recital supporting strategic recognition of high-value manufacturing sectors for their contribution to growth, innovation, employment, industrial heritage and quality and safety standards.
Adds reduced reliance on risky third-country technology suppliers, protection of sensitive industrial data and continuity of household and business energy supply to cybersecurity objectives.

Adds a recital extending security concerns beyond ICT to equipment controlling energy flows, opposing unilateral manufacturer, supplier or other third-party technical control capable of materially affecting its operation.

cat: Preference for trusted EU digital solutions
txt: Adds proportionate priority for EU-designed, developed, maintained or controlled software, control systems, updates, maintenance and remote-access solutions alongside high-risk-supplier exclusions.
Adds urgent intervention and appropriate corrective solutions, including transnational and cross-border cooperation where necessary.

cat: Trusted European digital energy value chains
txt: Adds a recital favouring EU-developed or controlled digital components, software and services where proportionate and internationally compatible, reducing dependencies and protecting sensitive industrial data.

cat: EU control of critical energy equipment
txt: Adds a recital supporting effective EU-jurisdiction control over critical commands and software changes regardless of supplier origin, with safe essential operation if external supplier services fail.
Adds capacity mechanisms exclusively deploying net-zero technologies and removes the obsolete 30% comparison in the recital's coverage rationale.
Deletes the obsolete reference to 'not only to 30%, but', leaving the recital's expanded coverage statement without that comparison.
Adds low-carbon technologies alongside the net-zero coverage in the recital on the relevant industrial framework.
Deletes the recital supporting origin requirements for nuclear plant construction and hydrogen-electrolyser manufacturing support under the Net-Zero Industry Act.
Deletes the recital supporting origin requirements for nuclear plant construction and hydrogen-electrolyser manufacturing support under the Net-Zero Industry Act.

Adds protection for advanced nuclear projects and qualifying OECD nuclear-cooperation partners, while excluding Russian, Belarusian and specified distorted or subsidised sources from new component contracts, including in advanced projects.

cat: Removal of nuclear construction origin rationale
txt: Deletes nuclear-plant construction and the associated EU-sovereignty rationale, retaining the recital's origin requirement rationale for hydrogen-electrolyser manufacturing support.

Adds supply availability and excludes advanced nuclear projects already receiving a positive Euratom Article 41 Commission opinion from origin requirements, seeking to avoid costs, delays and bottlenecks.

Adds supply availability and excludes advanced nuclear projects already receiving a positive Euratom Article 41 Commission opinion from origin requirements, seeking to avoid costs, delays and bottlenecks.

Adds supply availability and excludes advanced nuclear projects already receiving a positive Euratom Article 41 Commission opinion from origin requirements, seeking to avoid costs, delays and bottlenecks.

Adds supply availability and excludes advanced nuclear projects already receiving a positive Euratom Article 41 Commission opinion from origin requirements, seeking to avoid costs, delays and bottlenecks.

cat: Whole-project EU content in nuclear power
txt: Replaces the component-only approach with project-specific assessment of intellectual property, manufacturing, EU value added, workforce and long-term maintenance and service contracts.

cat: Third-country nuclear technologies and supply security
txt: Adds protection of energy supply and priority access to third-country cutting-edge nuclear technologies, particularly small modular reactors.
Adds equal treatment for components from trusted third-country partners and calls for corresponding Net-Zero Industry Act changes.

cat: Increasing EU nuclear content and know-how
txt: Replaces a best-efforts preference with a substantial and increasing EU-content ambition and adds know-how to the elements expected to remain European.

cat: Hydrogen use, electrolyser stacks and natural hydrogen
txt: Refocuses hydrogen on hard-to-electrify sectors, highlights strategic electrolyser-stack origin and calls for assessment of naturally occurring hydrogen within the net-zero technology framework.
Adds competitive EU hydrogen production, renewable and low-carbon use in hard-to-abate sectors, infrastructure development, electrolyser supply chains, skills and innovation.
Adds particular attention to electrolyser-stack origin and calls for rapid adjustment of the hydrogen strategy and supporting legislation for European industrial scale-up.
Broadens the gigawatt-electrolyser deployment rationale to a technology-neutral EU hydrogen sector, including research and responsible development of other domestic low-carbon hydrogen sources.
Adds technological neutrality between solutions contributing to EU decarbonisation and softens the recital's description of a single pathway as essential.

Adds a recital linking hydrogen, geothermal and rare-metal development to former mining and industrial regions, supporting responsibly developed natural hydrogen, EU geological resources and associated industrial skills.
Adds a recital calling for reduced dependence in transmission and distribution cables and advanced connectivity technologies to reinforce energy sovereignty and supply security.
Adds assurance of component availability over the medium and long term to the relevant net-zero technology manufacturing rationale.
Deletes the recital supporting removal of conditions restricting Commission environmental sustainability labelling powers for construction products.
Deletes the recital supporting removal of conditions restricting Commission environmental sustainability labelling powers for construction products.
Deletes the recital supporting removal of conditions restricting Commission environmental sustainability labelling powers for construction products.
Deletes the call to remove the existing restrictions on Commission labelling powers, retaining the description of consumer-choice and installation-dependent environmental-performance conditions.
Deletes the call to remove the existing restrictions on Commission labelling powers, retaining the description of consumer-choice and installation-dependent environmental-performance conditions.
Adds a recital supporting delegated Commission powers over third countries whose net-zero product content is treated as equivalent to EU origin.
Adds a recital supporting reuse of available data and protection against de facto exclusion of SMEs, local producers and European material suppliers with verifiable environmental performance.
Adds safeguarding and strengthening economic security to the objectives justifying EU-level action under subsidiarity.
Adds economic security alongside resilient and decarbonised industrial production in the statement of objectives supporting EU-level action.
Replaces 'decarbonised' with 'competitive' in the recital's description of the industrial production objective.
Deletes the claim that Member States cannot sufficiently achieve the objective alone and adds support for EU production without disproportionate administrative burdens.
Adds a recital calling for urgent inclusion of wind converters, electrolyser rectifiers and additional wind components in the net-zero resilience implementing list.

Adds a recital supporting tightly controlled equivalent treatment for selected content from associated overseas territories, citing Greenland and New Caledonia, without changing customs origin status.
Adds a recital supporting Commission action plans with sector-specific objectives, implementation pathways and coordinated EU instruments, reflecting regional ecosystems and SME needs.
Adds a recital calling for implementation to reflect remoteness, insularity, regional sourcing, energy, logistics, water, waste and land constraints and support local production and resilience.
Adds a recital calling for implementation to reflect remoteness, insularity, regional sourcing, energy, logistics, water, waste and land constraints and support local production and resilience.
Adds a recital calling for implementation to reflect remoteness, insularity, regional sourcing, energy, logistics, water, waste and land constraints and support local production and resilience.
Adds a recital requiring consultation of Parliament, Member States, social partners, industry, SMEs and other stakeholders when reviewing the Regulation.

Expands Article 1's objectives to imported-emissions reduction, resource efficiency, carbon-leakage prevention and industrial sovereignty, balancing decarbonisation with competitiveness, continued production and supply security.

cat: Existing industrial capacity and investment conditions
txt: Adds preservation and modernisation of the existing industrial base, investment attractiveness, technology neutrality, lower burdens and competitive energy, raw-material access and regulatory stability to Article 1.

cat: Productivity, fair competition and defence readiness
txt: Adds productivity and capacity growth, reduced high-risk dependencies, fair competition with third-country producers, SME investment and defence readiness to the Regulation's objectives.
Adds a diagnosis of weakened competitiveness caused by inconsistent EU policies and excessive burdens and makes restoration of a level playing field with third-country competitors an objective.
Adds decarbonisation, electrification, circularity, resource efficiency, energy sovereignty and public order to the objectives, broadening the original climate and competitiveness formulation.

cat: Energy security and harmonised investment conditions
txt: Adds a harmonised level playing field, energy security and self-sufficiency, investment attractiveness and avoidance of unnecessary administrative burdens.
Adds explicit protection of subsidiarity, affordability, supply security and proportionality while strengthening the business case for EU investment, innovation and production.
Adds explicit protection of subsidiarity, affordability, supply security and proportionality while strengthening the business case for EU investment, innovation and production.
Adds decarbonisation, circularity, resource efficiency, wider environmental objectives, energy affordability and security, and the do-no-significant-harm principle to Article 1.

cat: Energy security and avoidance of duplicate permitting
txt: Adds energy security and self-sufficiency and prohibits parallel or additional permitting regimes where equivalent EU or national procedures already exist.

cat: Cohesion and distribution of industrial benefits
txt: Adds economic, social and territorial cohesion and balanced distribution of industrial development benefits between Member States and regions.

cat: Harmonised investment conditions and burden reduction
txt: Adds a harmonised level playing field, investment attractiveness and avoidance of unnecessary administrative burdens to Article 1's objectives.

cat: Reshoring and expansion of EU manufacturing
txt: Adds facilitation of relocation to the EU and establishment or expansion of manufacturing within it as an explicit objective.
Adds that the Regulation must not create parallel or additional permitting regimes where equivalent EU or national procedures already exist.
Adds secure, affordable energy and reduction of industrial development gaps between Member States and regions.
Adds decarbonisation expressly to Article 1's statement of the Regulation's objectives.
Replaces the reference to the EU climate objective with energy objectives in Article 1's purpose clause.
Removes the internal-market framework formulation and states competitiveness and resilience more directly, adding productive investment in the EU green economy.
Deletes the EU climate objective from Article 1's stated purposes while retaining the other industrial and economic aims.

cat: Enabling conditions and national energy choices
txt: Adds binding duties for EU and national action to support competitive energy, raw-material access and regulatory predictability, respect technology neutrality and preserve Member States' Treaty-based energy choices.
Adds proportionate and technology-neutral implementation to the general description of the Regulation's measures.
Replaces the decarbonisation-project wording with industrial improvement and upgrading for efficiency, broadening the permitting measure's stated scope.
Adds streamlining of the permit-application process to the measures described in Article 1.
Adds simplification alongside acceleration to the permitting measures described in Article 1.
Replaces the decarbonisation-only reference with joint energy-intensive industry and clean-technology projects in the description of permitting measures.
Replaces 'speed-up' with 'facilitate' in the permitting objective, softening the emphasis on accelerated procedures.
Replaces the decarbonisation-project qualification with strategic-project wording, broadening the permitting objective beyond emissions-reduction projects.

cat: Positive incentives and broader production standards
txt: Recasts lead-market measures around positive demand incentives and proportionate production standards, adds auctions and prevents low-carbon performance becoming the sole or predominant criterion.

cat: Sustainable-carbon requirements for chemicals and plastics
txt: Adds sustainable-carbon-source requirements for chemical and plastic products as an additional instrument alongside origin and low-carbon conditions.

cat: Sustainable-source requirements for chemicals and plastics
txt: Adds sustainable-source requirements for chemical and plastic products and allows combinations with origin and low-carbon requirements.

cat: Combined demand requirements and labour compliance
txt: Strengthens the combination of origin and low-carbon demand measures and adds strict compliance with applicable social and labour-law obligations.
Adds requirements concerning sustainable carbon sources where appropriate, allowing combinations with origin and low-carbon conditions.

cat: Combined demand requirements and labour compliance
txt: Combines origin and low-carbon lead-market objectives and adds compliance with applicable social and labour-law obligations.
Adds sustainable-carbon-source requirements and support for EU producers to the demand-measure objective, replacing the original either-or formulation.
Adds sustainable-carbon-source requirements to the possible combinations of industrial demand measures.
Adds sustainable-carbon-source requirements and support for EU producers alongside the origin and low-carbon instruments.
Adds sustainable-carbon-source requirements and allows combinations with the existing origin and low-carbon measures.
Replaces the option of applying either origin or low-carbon requirements, or both, with wording combining the two requirements.
Adds that foreign investments must produce effective, verifiable and lasting benefits for host territories through productive capacity, industrial employment and know-how transfer within the EU.

cat: Limited rather than emerging investment sectors
txt: Replaces emerging sectors with a limited number of strategic sectors, removing the maturity-based restriction while retaining a constrained sectoral scope.

cat: Targeted rather than emerging investment sectors
txt: Replaces the emerging-sector limitation with targeted strategic sectors, permitting coverage of established activities where selected.

cat: Targeted rather than emerging investment sectors
txt: Replaces the emerging-sector limitation with targeted strategic sectors, permitting coverage of established activities where selected.

cat: Selected rather than emerging investment sectors
txt: Replaces emerging strategic sectors with selected sectors, removing maturity as the defining scope limitation.

cat: Targeted rather than emerging investment sectors
txt: Replaces the emerging-sector limitation with targeted strategic sectors, allowing coverage to follow strategic selection rather than sectoral maturity.
Deletes the emerging-sector limitation from Article 1's description of foreign-investment conditions.

ref: Article premier – paragraph 2 – point c a (new)
txt: Adds application of Chapter IV conditions to other strategically important industries, including established sectors and those with lost or insufficient EU production capacity.
Recasts the designation measure as Member State provision, where appropriate, for at least one industrial acceleration area.

cat: Strategic manufacturing focus of acceleration areas
txt: Replaces general industrial activities with manufacturing in strategic sectors, narrowing the stated area-development focus.
Replaces designation with encouragement of voluntary designation, weakening the compulsory character of the Article 1 measure.
Adds preservation and creation of quality employment through compliance with EU, national, collective-agreement and relevant international social and labour rules as an express measure.

ref: Article premier – paragraph 2 – point d a (new)
txt: Adds strengthening trade-defence instruments and activating sectoral safeguards where unfair competition threatens European industrial sovereignty.
Adds regional, national and EU supply-chain resilience and security as an express measure under the Regulation.

cat: Necessity and proportionality of market restrictions
txt: Adds an overarching openness principle and restricts market, procurement, support and investment limitations to necessary, proportionate responses to demonstrated risks, excluding unaffected sectors and investments.

Adds protection against disproportionate costs, delays, shortages and burdens and confines origin and lead-market duties to expressly covered public procurement and support, excluding mandatory private-procurement requirements.
Adds proportionate, technology-neutral implementation, non-discrimination between Member States' operators and safeguards for national security, energy choices and Treaty defence interests.
Requires the Commission to adopt sectoral and value-chain action plans coordinating objectives and implementation with the mobilisation and adaptation of EU instruments.
Adds an express safeguard preserving each Member State's responsibility for national security under Article 4(2) TEU.
Adds an express safeguard preserving each Member State's responsibility for national security under Article 4(2) TEU.
Requires all implementing measures to respect specified WTO and EU trade commitments and obliges the Commission to propose prompt correction where it identifies inconsistency.

Adds protection against disproportionate costs, delays, shortages and burdens and confines origin and lead-market duties to expressly covered public procurement and support, excluding mandatory private purchasing requirements.
Deletes Article 2 in its entirety, removing the objective that manufacturing account for at least 20% of EU GDP by 2035.
Adds decarbonisation to Article 2's title, framing the provision as covering both industrialisation and emissions-reduction objectives.
Deletes the paragraph setting the 20%-of-EU-GDP manufacturing objective for 2035.
Deletes the paragraph setting the 20%-of-EU-GDP manufacturing objective for 2035.
Deletes the paragraph setting the 20%-of-EU-GDP manufacturing objective for 2035.

cat: 25% target and genuine domestic industrial gains
txt: Raises the target from 20% to 25% and adds safeguards for net EU capacity gains, reshoring and EU control of strategic assets, opposing increased dependencies or simple relocation between Member States.

Retains the industrialisation ambition with stronger environmental safeguards and adds a 2035 objective for renewable electricity to provide at least 50% of industrial final energy consumption, supported by expanded grids.

Adds geographically balanced industrial investment and a seven-year extension of general deadlines for below-average-GDP Member States with major structural investment gaps, linked to dedicated EU industrial-cohesion funding.

Adds policy-consistency review, competitive energy, diversified material and energy supplies and predictable proportionate regulation, implemented with technological neutrality, as means of pursuing the target.
Retains the 20%-of-GDP objective and adds a 50% electricity share of manufacturing final energy use by 2035, alongside Clean Industrial Deal and net-zero manufacturing benchmarks.

Links the manufacturing-share objective, particularly in strategic sectors, to climate and environmental goals, reduced dependencies, productivity and innovation, quality jobs and territorial and social convergence.
Strengthens the duty to take appropriate measures and expressly promotes establishment, expansion, retention and reshoring of EU manufacturing capacity, particularly in strategic sectors.

cat: Critical-sector capacity instead of GDP target
txt: Replaces the 20%-of-GDP-by-2035 target with competitiveness and strategic autonomy through retained manufacturing and know-how in critical sectors, subject to subsidiarity, affordability and proportionality.

cat: Productivity and investment instead of GDP target
txt: Replaces the quantified manufacturing-share target with competitiveness and resilience objectives pursued through productivity, productive investment, innovation, scale-up and reduced dependencies.
Softens the target wording to 'endeavour' and requires Commission and national policies to consider predictable and competitive energy prices.

Prioritises European countries, especially EEA, EFTA and UK partners, when granting equivalence, reflecting integration into EU value chains.

Adds Article 9a requiring review of regulatory obstacles within 12 months and, where appropriate, harmonised end-of-waste criteria for strategic recycled materials.
Adds Article 9a requiring EU melt and pour for CN Chapters 72–73 and applying existing steel origin-evidence and verification rules.
Adds Article 9a requiring a free updated country-equivalence tool within six months, linked to the proposed Public Procurement Act tool.
Adds Article 9b allowing investigation of artificial trade/production changes and exclusion of products or operators; the draft retains placeholders for timing and procedure references.
Adds Article 9b requiring proportionate intra-EU waste-shipment procedures and Commission guidance, preserving traceability, environmental controls and action against illegal shipments.

Requires consideration of applicable international CO2 labelling schemes when setting low-carbon definitions.

Requires measurable technology-neutral criteria using ETS benchmarks and verified CBAM data, recognising recycled materials, secondary raw materials and scrap.

Requires cement, concrete, mortar and clinker methods to reflect plant emissions, material flows and actual energy, including relevant CCS and secondary materials; detached certificates alone cannot suffice.

a: Daniel Obajtek, Marion Maréchal, Anna Zalewska, Jadwiga Wiśniewska, Jacek Ozdoba
txt: Adds Union final assembly and component, traction/power-conversion and electronics/control/signalling shares for procured locomotives; all three percentage thresholds remain unspecified [X].
Retains alternative criteria and requires a year-four battery-capacity and consumer-price assessment before any proposal making them cumulative, including LFP supply.

a: Paolo Borchia, Isabella Tovaglieri, Raffaele Stancanelli, Klara Dostalova, Jana Nagyová, Ondřej Knotek, Jaroslav Bžoch, Tomáš Kubín
txt: Creates a new Part IIIa for zero/low-emission vehicle super credits, applying the annex's criteria by reference to the cited vehicle CO2 framework.

a: Pierre Jouvet, Raphaël Glucksmann, François Kalfon
txt: Adds procurement/support origin rules from six months: Union machine/battery assembly and design, 70% non-battery value and phased three/five battery components at years three/six, with tailored tower-crane rules.
